note: English version of data/academy.json (our review of the Academy content and Grok's conversation): overlay by lesson id, same shape. Educational, not investment advice.

lessons.title: Order flow tools: what can we trust?
lessons.verdict_note: Consistent with what we built in the Workspace (the order book gets pulled, executed trades are more honest). The ratings (high / medium) are the source's opinion from blog posts, not something we measured. The forward test of the zones has not produced a verdict yet.
lessons.summary: Executed trades (Time & Sales) and delta are more honest than the order book (DOM) because resting orders get pulled. The proposed logic: a level fixed in advance, then price arrives, then absorption, then entry.
points: DOM: the liquidity standing right now. Relatively lower trust because those orders get pulled.
Time & Sales: who actually traded. High trust.
Order tracker (PLACED / PULLED / FILLED): separates an order that was executed from one that was pulled. Medium trust because snapshots come only about every 20 seconds.
Heatmap: liquidity over time. Medium trust.
Footprint and delta: the aggression inside the candle. High trust when aggressor data exists.
Pressure counter: net of the last two minutes. Good for timing.
caveats: Every rating comes from educational sources and was not measured on our data.
A full traditional footprint (bid x ask at every price) is not complete on every market in our data.

lessons.title: Layers, not votes: the decision chain
lessons.verdict_note: The idea is reasonable, but the sentence "more than 4 families hurts" is attributed to the lab and I am not sure of it: my review of the lab found that not one row of the lab's chains passes the gate, so there is no positive evidence for any chain. Treat it as a hypothesis to test.
lessons.summary: Instead of counting how many indicators agree, go in order: market state, then the higher timeframe, then location (level / zone), then the trigger, then order flow, then timing, then the plan.
points: Each layer answers a different question and must pass before the next one.
Many agreeing families are not necessarily stronger evidence if they measure the same thing.
The Radar applies this gradually: a market-state strip, filters, and trade cards for the confirmed ones.
caveats: We have no test showing that this ordering raises profit.

lessons.title: Sessions and Kill Zones (Asia, London, New York)
lessons.verdict_note: The times come from educational ICT blogs and we have no statistical test showing that this timing makes a difference. Do not treat it as a rule before we test it on our own data. Caution: the times are New York time and shift with daylight saving.
lessons.summary: Asia builds a range, London sweeps liquidity or makes the first move, the London-New York overlap has the highest liquidity, and New York continues or reverses.
points: Asia is about 20:00-00:00 New York time.
New York morning is about 07:00-10:00, and the overlap is about 08:00-12:00.
The Workspace already has session boxes and Kill Zones.
caveats: The times are approximate and differ between sources.
Do not treat it as a profit filter before testing.

lessons.title: Claim check: "the lab's best strategies"
lessons.verdict_note: Grok listed as best: turtle55, sma1040, liqline 1d, m2022 1d and ohl_break 1d, and said the Lab has no costs. My review: the cost exists (0.1R) and not one of the detectors passes the gate (n >= 100, t > 3, positive net, both halves positive). The detector rows have no t at all (0 of 186), and the chain rows do have t (221) and none of them passes. The first frozen test (holdout) is not evidence either. So this ranking must not be shown as evidence. One more note: the docs/academy/ai files carry lab_status: primary_candidate for trend and per_pattern for harmonic. That means under test, not success.
lessons.summary: The numbers in the conversation about "the best" must not be turned into a recommendation. Our yardstick is the statistical gate in the lab, and so far no detector has passed it.
points: The gate: n >= 100, t > 3, positive net after cost, and both halves positive.
The cost charged is 0.1R per trade.
Lab detectors: 0 of 186 have a t-stat. Chains: 221 have a t, and none passes.
caveats: If the lab is re-run with more markets the result may change. It must be reviewed again.
